domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: A single employee leave request; the subject of the cancellation flow. cancelledBy/cancelledAt record who cancelled and when (null until cancelled).

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Per-employee, per-leave-type, per-period balance. Cancellation releases reserved (pendingDays) or used (usedDays) days back to the employee.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of every state-changing operation, including cancellation (action CANCEL).

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Notifies the affected employee when their request is cancelled.

business_rules: An employee may cancel their own leave request only while it is DRAFT or SUBMITTED; a manager may cancel an APPROVED request only for their direct report (ADMIN may cancel any APPROVED request). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation authorization appears, not only here]

Cancelling a DRAFT request releases no balance days (nothing was reserved). Cancelling a SUBMITTED request decrements pendingDays by requestedDays. Cancelling an APPROVED request decrements usedDays by requestedDays. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance release on cancellation appears, not only here]

requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 (inclusive calendar days) is the single canonical day-count derivation used everywhere, including the balance release on cancellation. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever requestedDays appears, not only here]

Every state-changing operation, including cancellation, writes an AuditLog entry (action CANCEL) capturing beforeState and afterState. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever AuditLog appears, not only here]

Cancellation is only valid from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED states; a REJECTED or already-CANCELLED request cannot be cancelled (ConflictError). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation state guard appears, not only here]

Cancelling an APPROVED request must not drive usedDays below zero; the release is capped at requestedDays and the balance counters are asserted non-negative. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance non-negative counters appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
Cancellation flow domain slice. New lifecycle state CANCELLED already exists canonically on LeaveRequest (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) — no new state is introduced, but the CANCELLED transition is now defined. LeaveRequest gains two attributes: cancelledBy (string | null) and cancelledAt (Date | null), populated on cancellation to capture who cancelled and when (mirrors approverId/decidedAt). LeaveBalance lifecycle (OPEN/CLOSED, inferred from period dates) is unchanged; cancellation mutates its counters. AuditLog (RECORDED) and Notification (PENDING/SENT/READ/ARCHIVED) are reused unchanged.

Cancellation authorization (broad): employee cancels own DRAFT/SUBMITTED; manager cancels APPROVED for direct report; ADMIN cancels any APPROVED. Balance release (broad): DRAFT releases nothing; SUBMITTED decrements pendingDays by requestedDays; APPROVED decrements usedDays by requestedDays. The canonical inclusive day-count (requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1) is reused for the release amount — no new day-count derivation. Cancellation is guarded to DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED only (REJECTED/CANCELLED → ConflictError), writes a CANCEL AuditLog entry, and notifies the affected employee. Balance counters must remain non-negative.

Two open questions remain for the chief architect: (1) whether APPROVED cancellation is permitted after startDate/endDate has passed, and (2) whether the usedDays release is full or pro-rated when the leave has partially elapsed. These affect the cancellation guard and the exact release amount.

open_questions.question: Should a manager be allowed to cancel an APPROVED request after the leave start date has already passed (or after it has fully elapsed)?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the cancellation guard must compare startDate/endDate against the current date, and whether a partially-consumed leave can be cancelled at all.
candidate_options: Allow cancellation any time before endDate

open_questions.question: When cancelling an APPROVED request that has already partially elapsed, should the released usedDays be pro-rated to only the unelapsed portion, or released in full?
open_questions.impact: Affects the exact usedDays decrement amount and whether a partial-day/elapsed-day calculation is needed beyond the canonical requestedDays.
candidate_options: Release full requestedDays regardless of elapsed time
Release only the unelapsed calendar days
Disallow cancellation once any day has elapsed
